# GPTZero Performance in Identifying Artificial Intelligence-Generated Medical Texts: A Preliminary Study
## Abstract
### Results
GPTZero had a sensitivity of 0.65 (95% confidence interval, 0.41–0.85); specificity, 0.90 (0.73–0.98); accuracy, 0.80 (0.66–0.90); and positive and negative likelihood ratios, 6.5 (2.1–19.9) and 0.4 (0.2–0.7), respectively.

## RESULTS
[37](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10519776/#B37) GPTZero had an accuracy of 0.80 (95% CI, 0.66–0.90).

## DISCUSSION
In identifying AI-generated texts, GPTZero had an accuracy of 80%. GPTZero classifies a piece of text based on its perplexity score (a measure of text randomness; a lower score is in favor of AI-generated text) and burstiness score (a measure of the variation in perplexity). For instance, if the perplexity cut-off score is set to a lower value, the _Se_ will increase and lower false-negative results will ensue.

Like every highly specific test, GPTZero with its low false-positive rate, is more appropriate for ruling in rather than ruling out suspicious texts — if GPTZero classifies a text as AI-generated (a positive result), the result is very likely to be correct as it is unlikely to be false-positive.

GPTZero has a low (10%) false-positive (classifying a human-written text as AI-generated) and a high (35%) false-negative rate (classifying an AI-generated text as human-written).

web.title: What is perplexity & burstiness for AI detection? - GPTZero
web.description:
_Update: As of autumn 2023, GPTZero no longer uses perplexity and burstiness for its AI detection because we migrated to a deep-learning based architecture._

![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/93/d8/93d84efe-2017-4168-9591-b749ab8330d5/content/images/2023/07/Screen-Shot-2023-07-07-at-10.59.41-PM.png)Figure 1: Anderson Cooper asking what is perplexity and burstiness

**What is Perplexity and Burstiness**

The statistical layer of GPTZero’s AI detection model is composed of a ‘perplexity’ and ‘burstiness’ calculation — together they form the first layer for GPTZero’s AI detection.

One aspect of GPTZero’s algorithm uses an AI model similar to language models like ChatGPT to measure the perplexity of the given document.

On the other hand, if the next word that followed was “potato”, then that sentence would have much higher perplexity, and also a greater likelihood of being written by a human.

Burstiness, on the other hand, is a measure of how much writing patterns and text perplexities vary over the entire document.

Compared to other statistical methods for AI detection, burstiness is a key factor unique to GPTZero detector, allowing our models to evaluate long-term-context, and perform better with additional inputs.

- [GPTZero](https://gptzero.me/news/tag/gptzero/)

web.title: Why Perplexity and Burstiness Fail to Detect AI - Pangram
web.description:
When you search online for how AI detectors work, you'll typically see many sources citing the terms "perplexity" and "burstiness". We'll also get into the understanding of why they don't work, and why perplexity and burstiness based detectors falsely cite the Declaration of Independence as AI-generated, and why these detectors are also biased against nonnative English speakers.

## What are perplexity and burstiness?
For example, here are two sentences.

Okay, great, so what about burstiness? Burstiness is the change in perplexity over the course of a document. If some surprising words and phrases are interspersed throughout the document, we would say that it is high in burstiness.

## How do perplexity and burstiness based detectors work?
We just do not believe that they can work reliably in high stakes settings where inaccuracies must be avoided, such as in the classroom, where a false positive AI detection can potentially undermine trust between the teacher and the student, or even worse, create inaccurate evidence in a legal case.

## Shortcoming #1: Text in the Training Set is Falsely Classified as AI
And because the text is exactly the same every time it is seen during training, the model can memorize what the Declaration of Independence is when it sees it, and then automatically assign all of the tokens a very low perplexity, which then also makes the burstiness really low too.

Similarly, we find that other common sources of LLM training data also see elevated false positive rates with perplexity and burstiness detectors.

## Shortcoming #5: Perplexity-based Detectors Cannot Iteratively Self-Improve
That is how we have gotten our false positive rate from 2%, to 1%, to 0.1%, and now down to 0.01%.
